messages:
michael: Quick RFC follow-up: I want to propose deprecating global penalty buckets in favor of per-tenant route-slices. Main goals: finer-grained cost/latency tradeoffs, easier canaries, fewer global oscillations. Thoughts?

anika: +1 on the intent. Need to understand how this changes SLO calc and risk of priority inversion. Per-tenant slices sound great, but could explode routing state if not bounded.

pete: Two quick concerns: 1) memory/lookup cost if we keep per-route weight vectors; 2) cache invalidation — when a slice changes, KV cache entries become stale. We should define a compatibility layer and migration plan.

ziya: Compatibility layer idea: introduce a 'slice_alias' mapping in the policy engine. Old policies map to aliases that resolve to one or more slices. Migration step1: alias points to legacy behavior. Step2: roll slices in, step3: flip alias. Minimal runtime changes during migration.

michael: I sketched a minimal DSL patch:
```
route "chat.generate" {
  slices: ["low-latency", "cost-optimized"]
  alias: "legacy-global"
}
policy "legacy-global" { weight: 1.0 }
```
Runtime resolves alias -> slices; engine evaluates slice-level capacity first then global fallbacks.

anika: Nice. We should also indicate guarantees: per-slice capacity buckets, preemptive fallback policy if slice saturates, and metrics for slice-level token cost, p50/p95 latency, and drop rate.

pete: Agree. One more: rollout semantics for canary. Suggest per-slice rollout flags that are independent from tenant config. That lets us test a new kernel/quantization on a slice for a subset of traffic.

ziya: Also: eviction semantics. If a slice is disabled mid-request, we must avoid double-charge or partial cache evictions. Propose a 'grace window' (X ms) where old slice still serves inflight requests and cache TTLs keep entries alive until safe.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://ci/infra/boards/4321 — includes telemetry dashboards, migration job, and canary automation.

michael: Action items: 1) Pete + Ziya to size lookup table and write eviction tests (ETA Tue). 2) Anika to update SLO calc doc with slice granularity (ETA Fri). 3) I'll draft RFC with DSL compat pattern and rollout plan (ETA end of week).

anika: one more nit: add automated regressions on quality for cost-optimized slices (embedding/chat output quality). we don't want cost wins with silent quality regressions. :eyes: 

pete: I'll add a quick eval hook in the rollout pipeline and a dashboard for quality deltas per-slice.

michael: Sweet. If no objections, I'll put RFC in docs repo later today and ping arch review.
